---
title: "Coupling"
---

The nationwide model is made in two stages.
`samenvoegen` merges the 22 models into one model file in which they are still separate, `lhm_parts`.
`koppelen` connects them where they meet, into `lhm_coupled`.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  hws["hws_transient"] --> merge
  gravity["11 &lt;authority&gt;_dynamic_model"] --> merge
  level["10 &lt;authority&gt;_forcing"] --> merge
  merge(["samenvoegen<br>08_samenvoegen_modellen.py"]) --> parts["lhm_parts"]
  parts --> couple(["koppelen<br>09_koppelen_modellen.py"])
  netwerk["netwerk.gpkg, Top10NL, OSM fairways"] --> couple
  peilbeheer["peilbeheer.gpkg"] --> couple
  couple --> coupled["lhm_coupled"]

  classDef step fill:#dfedef,stroke:#0c6a77
  class merge,couple step
```

## Merging

`pipeline/08_samenvoegen_modellen.py` reads each model, makes its IDs unique with `prefix_index`, see [Node IDs](index.qmd#sec-node-ids), and appends all its tables with `concat`.
The original IDs stay available in `meta_node_id_waterbeheerder` and `meta_link_id_waterbeheerder`, and `meta_waterbeheerder` holds the authority.
The merged model starts with the settings of the model of the main water system, and the solver settings are set here.

## Connecting the models

In each regional model, a LevelBoundary stands for the water on the other side of its border.
`AssignAuthorities` records whose water that is in the column `meta_couple_authority` of the node table, with `Noordzee` or `Buitenland` where it leaves the model.
The boundaries of the main water system have `Noordzee` or `Buitenland` as well, so they stay boundaries.

`process_boundary_nodes` then goes through the boundaries of the regional models:

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-cap: "What happens to a LevelBoundary with a `meta_couple_authority`."
flowchart TD
  start["LevelBoundary"] --> own{"Couples to its own authority,<br>Noordzee or Buitenland?"}
  own -->|yes| stays["Stays a boundary"]
  own -->|no| forced{"In forced_coupling?"}
  forced -->|yes| target["Connect to the given<br>Basin or Junction"]
  forced -->|no| near{"Boundaries of the other authority<br>within 20 m?"}
  near -->|"more than one"| stays
  near -->|one| pair{"Two Outlets in opposite directions,<br>both with or both without control?"}
  pair -->|yes| merged["Merge into one Outlet"]
  pair -->|no| basin
  near -->|none| basin["Connect to the nearest Basin / area<br>of the other authority"]
```

Connecting to the nearest Basin is the easiest and most common case. It relinks the connector nodes of the boundary, for instance an Outlet, so an inflow into the boundary becomes an outlet into the Basin, and an outflow becomes an inlet from it.
If a path in the opposite direction already exists, that path and the connector are removed instead, to avoid a cycle.
`replace_listen_node_id` points control nodes that listened to the boundary to the node that replaces it.
For the Basins of Rijkswaterstaat, the new link follows the topology of `Rijkswaterstaat/verwerkt/netwerk.gpkg`, instead of a direct line.
No new control nodes are added.

Two LevelBoundaries close to one another, especially between two water boards, are treated as duplicates, and merged if they meet the conditions above.

Where two Pumps, or an Outlet and a Pump, meet at a border, or Outlets do not meet these conditions, they are handled as a connector to a Basin.
That leaves duplicate connector nodes in place, and might duplicate a flow.
Still to do are couplings for `Pump | LevelBoundary . LevelBoundary | Pump` and `Pump | LevelBoundary . LevelBoundary | Outlet`, and investigating whether other connections happen.

::: {layout-ncol=2}
![Before coupling, in `lhm_parts`. Rijnland (green) and Amstel, Gooi en Vecht (blue) both end in LevelBoundaries (triangles) along their border.](https://s3.deltares.nl/ribasim-nl/doc-image/figures/coupling-before.png){fig-alt="Two authorities with several pairs of triangles along their border, each with links on one side."}

![After coupling, in `lhm_coupled`. Each pair of LevelBoundaries with the Outlets next to it is now one Outlet (square) with links to both sides.](https://s3.deltares.nl/ribasim-nl/doc-image/figures/coupling-after.png){fig-alt="The same area with squares on the border where the triangles were, and links that cross the border."}
:::

`forced_coupling` lists the exceptions, usually with an issue that explains them.
For instance, LevelBoundary 1500551 of Delfland couples to Basin 4000298, the Brielse Meer, rather than to the nearest Basin in the Hartelkanaal.

## The other steps of `koppelen`

`couple_model` in `pipeline/09_koppelen_modellen.py` runs these steps in order:

1. **Remove the summer and winter levels**, since the coupling and its level check work with fixed levels, and the nodes listed in `remove_nodes`, mostly structures that belong to the neighbouring model and boundaries without a link.
2. **Replace the boundaries**, as above.
3. **Set names and levels** of the nodes where a boundary was a placeholder.
4. **Convert open connections**: `convert_outlets_to_manning_resistance` turns Outlets on open water, such as 1100600 Angstel-ARK ([#820](https://github.com/Deltares/Ribasim-NL/issues/820)), into ManningResistances.
5. **Fix profiles**: where an Outlet has a `min_upstream_level` below the bottom of the Basin upstream of it, the bottom of the Basin moves down.
6. **Remove invalid nodes**, with a warning: `remove_invalid_topology_nodes` removes nodes that the coupling left without a valid topology.
7. **Route the links** between models over Top10NL, with `netwerk.gpkg` as the main route. A link stays straight if it is listed in `straight_rws_links`, such as those of the Zeesluis Muiden ([#916](https://github.com/Deltares/Ribasim-NL/issues/916)).
8. **Add user demands** that cross models, such as the Evides drinking water of the Maasvlakte ([#857](https://github.com/Deltares/Ribasim-NL/issues/857)).
9. **Attach RWZIs** to the routes of Basins that only exist after coupling. For instance, RWZI Stein discharges to the Julianakanaal instead of a Basin of Limburg.
10. **Link observations** that measure on links between models, which need the coupled network, see `ribasim_nl.observations`.
11. **Tidy the layout**, see [Layout](layout.qmd), and link the observations that need the merged Junction trees.
12. **Write the model**, validate it with `validate_ribasim_nl`, and write the links that were added to `link.gpkg`.
13. **Correct the coupling levels**, see below.
14. **Apply the [summer and winter levels](seasonal-levels.qmd)** again, without changing the initial state, since the final state of the regional models already follows the seasons.

## Coupling levels

The connectors at a border must respect the target level of the Basin on the other side, which the regional model did not know.
`run_configured_coupling_level_check` corrects `min_upstream_level` and `max_downstream_level` of the Outlets and Pumps on links between authorities, and the thresholds of their DiscreteControl nodes.
The function of a connector follows from its capacity per control state.

| Limit | Applies to | Set to |
|:------|:-----------|:-------|
| `min_upstream_level` | outlet, or drain state of an inlet or flow control node | target level upstream |
| `min_upstream_level` | supply state of an inlet or flow control node | target level upstream − 0.04 m |
| `min_upstream_level` | inlet from Rijkswaterstaat | lowest level of the profile of the Basin + 0.1 m |
| `max_downstream_level` | supply state with capacity | target level downstream |

This is done for connectors of the 11 gravity controlled authorities (`COUPLING_LEVEL_APPLY_AUTHORITIES`), not for those of the level controlled authorities or Rijkswaterstaat, and rows with `meta_level_update_protected` or `meta_threshold_update_protected` opt out.
FlowDemand-controlled inlets stay untouched, with exceptions in Aa en Maas, De Dommel and Limburg.
See `ribasim_nl.coupling_levels`.

## After coupling

`koppelen` does not run the model.
`run_lhm_coupled` copies the model to `runs/lhm_coupled` and runs the first 2 of its 3 years, and `validate_lhm_coupled` [checks the results](../dev/testing.qmd#coupled-model-result-checks).
The [model viewer](../viewer.qmd) shows them, with the fit to the measurements.
